x: Marco Polo visited Motupalli port under Rudramadevi, Nicolo Conti came under Devaraya I, Nuniz described Vijayanagara under Achyutadeva Raya, and Abdul Razzaq came as envoy to Devaraya II's court, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Place each traveller by the ruler in whose reign he came.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Marco Polo
(b) Nicolo Conti
(c) Nuniz
(d) Abdul Razzaq

List-II
(i) Court of Devaraya II
(ii) Motupalli port
(iii) Vijayanagara under Achyutadeva Raya
(iv) Vijayanagara under Devaraya I

x: Option C is incorrect: Unnava Lakshminarayana visited Palnadu in July 1921 to study the Forest Satyagraha, not the Vandemataram Movement. Bipin Chandra Pal's Vandemataram tour and his stay with Ramadasu Naidu at Machilipatnam are right.
t: Check the movement in each statement.

x: Both are true: Bethanamathya was a patron of Jainism, and the Reddi ruler Veera Bhadra Reddy of Rajahmundry patronised the poet Srinatha.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Nicolo Conti, the Venetian merchant who visited Vijayanagara under Devaraya I around 1420, was the Italian. Nuniz was Portuguese, Abdul Razzaq Persian, and Marco Polo, though Italian, came to Motupalli in Kakatiya times, not Vijayanagara.
t: Recall the nationality of each traveller.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Tavernier was a gem merchant, and he travelled to Kollur because its mines were then a leading source of diamonds, including famous stones he described.
t: Ask whether the mines' fame in R is the motive for the visit in A.
s:
Assertion (A): The French jeweller Tavernier visited the Kollur mines in Andhra in the 17th century.
Reason (R): The Kollur mines were then among the world's chief sources of diamonds.

x: Both are true: the Italian Nicolo Conti visited South India under Devaraya I, and Abdul Razzaq came as the Persian envoy of Shah Rukh to the court of Devaraya II.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Tavernier visited the Andhra mines in the 17th century, Unnava Lakshminarayana toured Palnadu in July 1921, and Gandhi visited Hyderabad on 9 March 1934, giving A, B, C.
t: Arrange the events by period.

x: Two are linked with Jainism: the early Kakatiya kings and Bethanamathya. The Satavahana queens patronised Buddhism, and the Salankayanas were devotees of Chitrarathaswami, not patrons of Jainism.
t: Recall the faith each patron supported.

x: The Eastern Chalukya king Rajaraja Narendra patronised Nannayabhattu, who began the Telugu Mahabharata. Veera Bhadra Reddy patronised Srinatha.
t: Recall the patron of each poet.

x: Satavahana queens backed Buddhism, the Salankayanas worshipped Chitrarathaswami as their family deity, the early Kakatiya kings patronised Jainism, and Veera Bhadra Reddy the poet Srinatha, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall each dynasty's religious patronage, then the poet's patron.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Satavahana Queens
(b) Salankayanas
(c) Early Kakatiya Kings
(d) Veera Bhadra Reddy

List-II
(i) Jainism

(iv) Worship of Chitrarathaswami

x: I, II and III are correct: Gandhi visited Hyderabad in 1934 for Harijan uplift, Unnava Lakshminarayana studied the Forest Satyagraha in Palnadu in 1921, and Bipin Chandra Pal stayed with Ramadasu Naidu at Machilipatnam.
t: Check each statement separately.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Mahatma Gandhi visited Hyderabad for Harijan uplift work.
II. Unnava Lakshminarayana visited the Palnadu area to study the Forest Satyagraha.
III. Bipin Chandra Pal was a guest of Ramadasu Naidu at Machilipatnam.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Rudramadevi, who ruled from Orugallu (Warangal) and was praised by Marco Polo, belonged to the Kakatiya dynasty.
t: Recall the dynasty of the queen.

x: Motupalli, the Kakatiya port visited by Marco Polo, was also called Desiyakondapattanam. Vijayapuri is Nagarjunakonda, Vengipuram is Pedavegi and Pratipalapuram is Bhattiprolu.
t: Recall the other name of each place.

x: Vengipuram is present Pedavegi near Eluru, Vijayapuri is modern Nagarjunakonda, Koduru is the ancient name of Gudur, and Bhattiprolu was anciently Pratipalapuram, giving a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.
t: Recall the ancient and modern names.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Kakatiya gold coins were called Mada and caste associations Samayamu; the name of the associations has nothing to do with the coin's name.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Option C is incorrect: the severe Ganjam Famine is dated 1865–66, not 1866–67. Andhra Sivaji for Parvataneni Veerayya Choudary, Andhra Bhishma for Nyapathi Subba Rao and Andhra Ratna for Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya are right.
t: Check the years in each statement.

x: Both are true: the 1907 Rajahmundry College incident marked the start of student participation in the freedom struggle in Andhra, and the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement preceded the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Nagalapuram in Palnadu was known in ancient times as Hala. Pratipalapuram is Bhattiprolu, Desiyakondapattanam is Motupalli and Orugallu is Warangal.
t: Recall the ancient name of each place.

x: I and II are correct: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was called Andhra Ratna and Denabandhu. III is false because Harikatha Pitamaha was the title of Adibhatla Narayana Dasu.
t: Check the title in each statement.

x: Madhvacharya founded the Dvaita (dualism) school of Vedanta. Vichitrachitta was a title of Mahendravarman, Samayamu meant Kakatiya caste associations and Aradalam a cream used by Satavahana dancers.
t: Discriminate the philosophy from the other terms.

x: A is true: the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 was the pact made before the formation of Andhra Pradesh. B is false because Aradalam was the foundation cream used by Satavahana dancers.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All four are correct: Parvataneni Veerayya Choudary was Andhra Sivaji, Nyapathi Subba Rao Andhra Bhishma, Adibhatla Narayana Dasu Harikatha Pitamaha and the Pallava king Mahendravarman Vichitrachitta.
t: Check each title separately.

x: Vinukonda Vallabharaya's Kridabhiramam describes Kakatiya Orugallu as the abode of drama artists and actors. Samayamu, Aradalam and Dvaita are terms, not literary works.
t: Recall the work that describes Orugallu.

x: Gudur, anciently Koduru, lies in the Bandar (Machilipatnam) taluk of Krishna district. Pedavegi is near Eluru and Nagarjunakonda is the old Vijayapuri.
t: Recall the location of each place.

x: Sri Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529) was a contemporary of Babur, who founded Mughal rule in 1526. Samudragupta, Hala and Kharavela lived many centuries earlier.
t: Match the ruler to the same century.

x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam performed the first widow remarriage in Andhra in 1881, Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu led the anti-nautch campaign, Brahma Naidu established the Dasa Samaj, and the English built Fort St. George at Madrasapatnam, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Separate the two reformers by their signature campaigns.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) First widow remarriage in Andhra (1881)
(b) Anti-nautch campaign against the Bhogam system
(c) Dasa Samaj
(d) Fort St. George

List-II
(i) Kandukuri Veeresalingam
(ii) R. Venkataratnam
(iii) Brahma Naidu
(iv) English at Madrasapatnam

x: A is true: after taking Udayagiri, Krishnadevaraya carried the Balakrishna idol to Hampi. R is false because the English built Fort St. George at Madrasapatnam; Udayagiri was a Gajapati fort in Nellore.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Annamayya (1408–1503), the Tallapaka composer, was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha Raya of Vijayanagara. Srinatha and Pedakomati Vema Reddy belong to the earlier Reddi period and Babur to the 16th century.
t: Match the composer to the same period.

x: The Kakatiya ruler Prola Raju II is credited with the Swayambhu Devalayam and Kesavalayam inside Warangal Fort. Brahma Naidu, Krishnadevaraya and Veeresalingam belong to other contexts.
t: Recall the Kakatiya builder.
